hypothesis: A fixed eight-hour exit may retain more HYPE breakout profit than the active regime-supported extension while reducing post-soft-boundary giveback.
decision: Preserve the exact $25-notional fixed-eight-hour profile as a staged but inactive candidate. Do not activate it until every venue position and owned order is reconciled flat and a future live start receives explicit authority; compare its subsequent outcomes with the active extension contract without treating the staged file as runtime state.
falsifier: Causally complete profile-matched extension observations that consistently outperform their estimated fixed-eight-hour exits after fees, funding, and measured close friction would falsify the fixed-eight-hour hypothesis.
limitations: The extension comparison is sparse and contains contradictory resolved and unresolved observations.
An estimated historical soft-boundary close is not an actual submitted venue order.
A staged profile is not evidence that the running backend uses the candidate.
Activation requires a new mandatory pre-start backup and explicit live authority.
